headline_cluster.headline: שכר הדירה שוב זינק - וזה המחיר שתשלמו עכשיו תל אביב היא העיר היקרה ביותר, זינוק במחיר גם בירושלים

extracted_claims: Source: Central Bureau of Statistics (הלמ"ס), unfurnished rental apartments by city/room count
Biggest rise among 18 large cities: Beit Shemesh +11.6% to 5,078 NIS
Jerusalem: rose faster than average (no exact figure given), as in previous quarter too
Tel Aviv: most expensive, avg 7,488 NIS/month; 3.5-4 room apt 8,919 NIS, ~2.5x Be'er Sheva
Lowest average: Be'er Sheva 3,198 NIS, then Haifa, Ashkelon
Only decline in its group: Bat Yam 3.5-4 room apts -0.6%
National avg 3.5-4 room apts +1.8% to 5,497 NIS; 1-2 room apts +0.8%
CBS caveat noted in article: changes also reflect shifts in mix/quality of surveyed apartments, not pure price change
n12.refetch_2026-11-28: WebFetch of mako URL succeeded (raw curl returned a 225-byte compressed stub; no JSON-LD extractable). Re-fetched body matches the extracted claims; the article gives NO exact Jerusalem % or Jerusalem average; adds that Bat Yam -0.6% is the only decline in the 3.5-4 room group.

primary_source_search.source: CBS, Price Statistics Monthly No. 10/2026, Table 4.9 'Average Monthly Prices of Rent (NIS), by Residential District, Big Cities and Size Group (Rooms)'
primary_source_search.method: PDF retrieved via WebFetch, text extracted with pdftotext -layout; YoY = 2026 VII-IX vs 2025 VII-IX columns, computed by auditor.
primary_source_search.not_found: The CBS Hebrew press release (הודעה לתקשורת) text for Q3 2026 rents was NOT located (cbs.gov.il unreachable from curl; web search returned no match). CBS's own verbal characterization (e.g. 'moderate') is therefore unverified; the framing assessment rests on the table numbers only.

context_from_table.big_city_yoy_rank_q3_2026: Beit Shemesh 11.60, Herzliya 6.32, Rehovot 5.90, Hadera 5.86, Kfar Saba 5.79, Petah Tikva 5.46, Rishon 5.27, Bnei Brak 5.19, Netanya 5.18, Be'er Sheva 4.82, Ramat Gan 4.41, Ashkelon 4.19, Jerusalem 4.18, Haifa 3.91, Bat Yam 3.82, Holon 3.62, Tel Aviv 3.47, Ashdod 3.39

claims.claim_text: Headline: 'שכר הדירה שוב זינק' (rent jumped again)
claims.verified_figure: National Q3 2026 YoY +3.63%; QoQ +0.91%; YoY rate DOWN from +4.24% in Q2 and +4.09% in Q1; 3.5-4 rooms +1.78%, 1-2 rooms +0.81%
claims.note: The level figure is right, but 'jumped again' frames a deceleration as a surge: annual rent growth slowed in Q3 and the quarterly move was <1%. The most common apartment size rose only 1.8%. CBS press-release wording not located, so no claim about CBS's own adjective.

claims.claim_text: Headline: 'זינוק במחיר גם בירושלים' (price jump also in Jerusalem)
claims.verified_figure: Jerusalem city avg 5,410.5 NIS, +4.18% YoY (13th of 18 big cities), +1.18% QoQ
claims.note: Above the national +3.63%, but below 12 other big cities including Be'er Sheva (+4.82%); 'jump' is not proportionate.

claims.claim_text: Source: CBS unfurnished/free-market rental apartments by city and room count
National average rent Q3 2026: 5,132 NIS/month, +3.6% YoY
Biggest rise among 18 large cities: Beit Shemesh +11.6% to 5,078 NIS
claims.verified_figure: Bet Shemesh 4,549.9 -> 5,077.5 NIS, +11.60%; table lists exactly 18 big cities
claims.note: Note: Beit Shemesh has high sampling error (99) and no 1-2 room cell; not flagged in article.

claims.claim_text: Jerusalem rose faster than national average, as also in the previous quarter
claims.verified_figure: Q3: city +4.18% vs national +3.63% (true). Q2: city +4.13% vs national +4.24% (city BELOW); district +4.86% vs 4.24%; city 3.5-4 rooms +4.01% vs national 2.51%
claims.note: Q3 part accurate. 'Also previous quarter' holds for Jerusalem district or the 3.5-4 room group, but NOT for Jerusalem city's overall average; article does not state which metric. No exact Jerusalem % given in the article.

claims.claim_text: Tel Aviv is the most expensive city, average 7,488 NIS/month
claims.verified_figure: Tel Aviv 7,488.4 NIS; next Herzliya 6,834.1, Kfar Saba 6,236.6
claims.note: Tel Aviv is #1 in the overall average AND in every room group (1-2: 5,519.1; 2.5-3: 7,160.0; 3.5-4: 8,918.6; 4.5+: 11,432.0). Note Tel Aviv's own YoY rise (+3.47%) is below national and 17th of 18; headline juxtaposition with 'jumped' could mislead, but the level claim holds.

claims.claim_text: Tel Aviv 3.5-4 rooms almost 2.5x Be'er Sheva
claims.note: Actually slightly above 2.5x ('almost' understates trivially); within rounding.

claims.claim_text: Lowest average: Be'er Sheva 3,198 NIS, then Haifa and Ashkelon
claims.verified_figure: Be'er Sheva 3,197.9; Haifa 3,437.8; Ashkelon 3,708.2; next Hadera 4,106.7

claims.claim_text: Bat Yam 3.5-4 room apartments fell 0.6%, the only decline in that group
claims.verified_figure: 5,309.9 -> 5,279.1 NIS, -0.58%; all other big cities' 3.5-4 cells positive
claims.note: Other room groups do show declines (Holon 1-2 -2.87%, Netanya 1-2 -0.96%); Bat Yam overall +3.82%.
These modest figures undercut the headline 'jump' framing.

claims.claim_text: Caveat: CBS changes also reflect composition/quality of surveyed apartments
claims.verified_figure: Table 4.9 footnote (1): 'Prices in the various quarters include changes in the composition and quality of dwellings.'

note: No contradicted/unsupported/misinterpreted/cherry_picked claims. All body figures match CBS Table 4.9. Issues: headline framing overstated ('jumped again' during a YoY deceleration; 'jump in Jerusalem' for 13th-of-18 rise) and the Jerusalem previous-quarter clause is imprecise.
